Conclusion: The Court held that the respondent was entitled to all benefits to which he would have been normally entitled, had he been on duty during the period of suspension. The Court further held that the Manual on Disciplinary Action and Related Matters of UCO Bank governed the case and not Regulation 15(2) of the United Commercial Bank (Conduct and Discipline and Appeal) Regulation, 1976.

The employment exchange of Badagara (Kerala) sponsored candidates for Mahe, the employment exchange Yanam sponsored candidates and employment exchange Vishakhapattnam (AP) sponsored candidates for Yanam. After holding interview final Selection List was prepared and out of finally selected SC candidates, candidates had produced community certificates from the Governments of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala, based on which the revenue authority of Pondicherry had issued community certificates to them. The remaining candidates produced community certificates from the revenue authority of Pondicherry.

Issues: The issue was whether migrant SC candidates belonging to another State is eligible for appointment on post which is reserved for SC candidate for Union Territory (hereinafter for short UT) of Pondicherry and also for direction to appoint original inhabitants of Scheduled Caste origin belonging to UT of Pondicherry.

Ratio of the decision: The ratio of the decision was that the SC persons who migrated to UT of Pondicherry after the issuance of Presidential notification, which has specified Scheduled Castes in terms ofArticle 341of the Constitution cannot claim the benefit of reservation in the matter of employment in Pondicherry Government service.
